title: Closing the logarithmic regret gap in skill-based queue routing
short_statement: Learning unknown match rewards in a fixed skill-based queue has logarithmic lower bounds and polylogarithmic upper bounds. Can a stable policy attain logarithmic regret against the same slack-constrained benchmark?
open_problem: Close the gap between logarithmic lower bounds and the $O((\log t)^{2\beta})$ guarantee for every fixed $\beta>1$, under the stated positive-slack, nondegenerate, consistent-policy model. In particular, establish instance-dependent $O(\log t)$ regret, or a stronger lower bound for the same model.
background: In a bandit problem, choosing an action typically produces an immediate observation. In a queue, the observation arrives only after a compatible server has completed service, and changing a routing rule changes both congestion and the supply of future observations. The operational objective is therefore coupled to the statistical learning problem. Fixing a positive capacity slack isolates this difficulty from critical-load instability. The recent Stochastic Systems analysis uses vertices of a static routing polytope as actions and growing episodes to control transient queue behavior. Its logarithmic factors leave a concrete algorithmic question within an already specified stochastic model.
full_statement:
Fix a connected bipartite compatibility graph $E\subseteq[I]\times[J]$ with $|E|>I+J-1$. Type-$i$ customers arrive as independent Poisson processes of known rates $\lambda_i>0$. Server $j$ serves one customer at a time with independent exponential durations of known rate $\mu_j>0$, regardless of customer type. Initially empty, the system allows customers to wait for compatible servers. A completed type-$(i,j)$ service yields an independent Bernoulli reward of unknown mean $\theta_{ij}\in(0,1)$. Rewards are observed only at completion.

Choose a fixed known $\epsilon>0$ and define the routing polytope
$$\mathcal X_\epsilon=\{x\ge0:\ \sum_{j:(i,j)\in E}x_{ij}=\lambda_i,\quad\sum_{i:(i,j)\in E}x_{ij}\le\mu_j-\epsilon\}.$$
Assume $\sum_{i\in U}\lambda_i<\sum_{j\in\cup_{i\in U}\{j:(i,j)\in E\}}\mu_j$ for every nonempty $U\subseteq[I]$, feasibility, and the source's nondegenerate regime: all primal and dual feasible bases are nondegenerate and the optimum $x^\theta$ is unique. Choose $\epsilon$ small enough that the feasible bases at zero slack remain feasible. The benchmark is $v_\epsilon(\theta)=\max_{x\in\mathcal X_\epsilon}\sum_{(i,j)\in E}\theta_{ij}x_{ij}$, not the zero-slack value.

Let $D_{ij}(t)$ count completed services and define
$$R_\pi^\theta(t)=t v_\epsilon(\theta)-\sum_{(i,j)\in E}\theta_{ij}\mathbb E_\pi^\theta D_{ij}(t).$$
Policies are nonanticipative and must satisfy, on every admissible instance,
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\left[t\lambda_i-\sum_j\mathbb E_\pi^\theta D_{ij}(t)\right]<\infty,\qquad
\sum_i\mathbb E_\pi^\theta D_{ij}(t)\le t(\mu_j-\epsilon).$$
Also impose the source's consistency condition: for every admissible reward vector $\xi$, every line with $x_{ij}^\xi>0$, and every $b>0$, $\mathbb P_\pi^\xi(D_{ij}(t)<b\log t)\to0$.

Can one policy attain $R_\pi^\theta(t)=O(\log t)$ on every fixed nondegenerate instance, with an instance-dependent constant? Otherwise prove that a larger order is unavoidable in this same policy class. The dimension, positive slack, and reward gaps stay fixed as $t\to\infty$; a minimax bound or a result against $\mathcal X_0$ is a different question.
known_results:
Van Kempen, Sanders, Sloothaak, and Wolf (Stochastic Systems 16(2):140-164, 2026), Theorem 2, prove $O((\log t)^{2\beta})$ regret for every fixed $\beta>1$ for UCB Queue Routing with Bernoulli rewards and prescribed growing episode lengths. Theorem 1 gives an instance-dependent $\Omega(\log t)$ lower bound under stability, slack, and consistency conditions. Its change-of-measure argument requires admissible confusing reward alternatives; for bounded Bernoulli means this qualification must be checked rather than allowing alternatives outside $(0,1)$.

Section 4.5.2 explicitly proposes exploiting shared observations across routing actions to improve the dependence on the number of LP vertices. Section 4.5.4 explains why changing to the zero-slack benchmark adds a different loss. Neither numerical performance nor ordinary finite-armed UCB alone proves the desired queueing guarantee.

Remaining open problem. Attain logarithmic regret or prove an unavoidable larger order with these same assumptions and benchmark. This gap-closing question is an editorial inference from Theorems 1-2, not a quoted conjecture.

progress.summary: The published 2026 theorem gives a polylogarithmic upper bound. Logarithmic lower bounds apply with the source's consistency and identifiability assumptions; matching the orders is the target.

counterexample_rationale: The target is an asymptotic stochastic-control guarantee. Small simulations cannot certify a lower bound over all admissible learning policies.
alphaevolve_rationale: Policy search may suggest ways to share observations or shorten warmup periods, but asymptotic regret and stability need proof.

literature.synthesis: The learning lower bound and the constructive queueing upper bound use a common positive-slack routing benchmark but have different technical requirements. The upper bound accounts for switching transients and random numbers of completed observations. A better method may reuse observations across actions and avoid repeatedly paying a growing warmup cost. The lower bound must keep reward alternatives inside the chosen family. The target here is instance-dependent logarithmic regret at fixed slack, not a uniform guarantee in vanishing slack, and not a conjecture that every nondegenerate instance has the same positive lower-bound constant.

reviewed.ref: Sanne van Kempen, Jaron Sanders, Fiona Sloothaak, Maarten G. Wolf, 'Learning Payoffs While Routing in Skill-Based Queues', Stochastic Systems 16(2):140-164, 2026
reviewed.result: Theorems 1-2 give logarithmic lower and polylogarithmic upper bounds with explicit stability, slack, consistency, and nondegeneracy assumptions.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Exploit shared reward observations across routing vertices. Analyze switching transients directly or design a routing implementation with faster coupling. For lower bounds, use admissible Bernoulli alternatives and account for unfinished work.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: Keep the epsilon-slack LP benchmark, server-only service rates, completion-only reward feedback, consistency, and expected capacity constraints. Prove queue stability as well as regret. An epsilon-dependent bound cannot be treated as uniform when epsilon tends to zero. Do not use Bernoulli alternatives with means above one in a KL lower bound.

where_posed.text: Editorially extracted gap between Theorems 1 and 2 of van Kempen, Sanders, Sloothaak, and Wolf (2026); related improvement directions are explicit in the paper.
